extracted.intended_audience: prospective SSIR contributors, readers, and those researching the Stanford Social Innovation Review
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes Stanford Social Innovation Review's mission, target audience, and submission guidelines (accepted article types and typical online length). Useful for authors preparing work for SSIR's print or online editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — advance, educate, and inspire
rubrics_metrics.description: SSIR's mission is to advance, educate, and inspire the field of social innovation by seeking out, cultivating, and disseminating the best in research- and practice-based knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should align with the mission: contribute to the field of social innovation and convey research- and practice-based knowledge that advances thinking or practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea quality — interesting, original, and important
rubrics_metrics.description: SSIR seeks to present interesting, original, and important ideas about social innovation to leaders who can put those ideas to work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should introduce ideas that are novel or present existing ideas in new, consequential ways; they should matter to practitioners and decision-makers who can implement them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience fit — written for social change leaders and cross-sector practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: SSIR is written by and for social change leaders from around the world and from all sectors of society—nonprofits, foundations, business, government, and engaged citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should target content and tone toward senior/operational leaders and practitioners across sectors who are able to act on the ideas presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence orientation — research- and practice-based knowledge; bridge research, theory, and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: With print and online articles, webinars, conferences, podcasts, and more, SSIR bridges research, theory, and practice on a wide range of topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred submissions will link theory and research to practical application; empirical grounding or clear practice-based insights are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical relevance — cross-sector solutions and topics like human rights, impact investing, nonprofit business models
rubrics_metrics.description: SSIR covers cross-sector solutions to global problems and a wide range of topics, including human rights, impact investing, and nonprofit business models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch topics that address systemic or cross-sector challenges in social innovation or that illuminate models, tools, or evidence applicable across sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted article types — six editorial categories for print
rubrics_metrics.description: SSIR accepts submissions for six types of editorial articles (Book Review, Case Study, Feature, Field Report, Viewpoint, and What's Next) for their quarterly print edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should select the submission category that matches their piece's purpose and format (e.g., submit empirical or descriptive organizational analysis as a Case Study; opinion or argument pieces as Viewpoint).

rubrics_metrics.name: Online pieces — typical length guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: SSIR accepts submissions of shorter works to be published online—typically of 1,200 to 2,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online submissions should generally aim for the 1,200–2,000 word range unless other length guidance is provided; adhere to SSIR's shorter-work expectations for the web.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication format and cadence — quarterly print edition and other formats
rubrics_metrics.description: SSIR is a magazine and website; it publishes a quarterly print edition and also produces webinars, conferences, podcasts, and in-depth series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider which format (print feature, shorter online piece, webinar accompaniment, or in-depth partnered series) best suits your submission and whether timing aligns with the quarterly cadence for print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative/partnered content — in-depth series often produced with partners
rubrics_metrics.description: SSIR frequently publishes in-depth series in partnership with organizations such as the Bridgespan Group, Mission Investors Exchange, BBB's Give.org, Third Sector Capital Partners, and The Communications Network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SSIR sometimes commissions or co-produces series with external organizations; prospective contributors should note that multi-article series and partnered projects are part of SSIR's publishing approach.
